data.title: US lawmakers propose up to 30% rewards for prediction market whistleblowers
data.description:
Two US lawmakers have proposed paying whistleblowers up to 30% of monetary sanctions in qualifying prediction market fraud cases, seeking tips about suspected insider trading.

On Friday, Democratic Representatives Sean Casten and Ted Lieu announced the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act of 2026. The bill would establish a Department of Justice program rewarding people whose original information helps resolve enforcement actions.

Under the proposal, whistleblowers would receive 10% to 30% of monetary sanctions from covered federal fraud cases involving prediction market platforms, provided that the sanctions exceed $1 million. The rewards would come from the DOJ’s Assets Forfeiture Fund, with the Attorney General determining payouts based on the significance of information and assistance.

The bill would permit anonymous submissions through lawyers and prohibit employer retaliation against whistleblowers.

The lawmakers cited concerns about government insiders profiting from bets on military operations and presidential speeches, including on platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket.

The latest proposal follows Senate passage of the DEATH BETS Act on Thursday, which would prohibit federally regulated prediction markets from offering contracts tied to war, assassination, terrorism and death.

In March, lawmakers introduced separate legislation to prevent officials from using nonpublic information to trade prediction market contracts. In May, House lawmakers sought records from Kalshi and Polymarket over suspected insider trading linked to military actions.

data.title: Iran Reportedly Wants Diplomacy To End War, But Trump Says ‘They Don’t Want To Make A Deal That’s Acceptable To Me’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Araghchi added that Iran was seeking an agreement with the U.S. that would ensure that there would be “no further war.”
  • He said that Iran is also seeking guarantees that the U.S. was earnest with respect to negotiations with the country.
  • Araghchi also clarified that one of Tehran’s red lines is the country keeping its highly enriched uranium, while noting that Iran was open to discussing a “fair solution.”

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi reportedly said that Iran wants diplomacy to end the ongoing war with the U.S. and Israel.

According to a Reuters report citing Araghchi’s comments to an Iranian newspaper, Iran’s Foreign Minister confirmed that talks with the U.S. were ongoing through mediators.

Tehran Seeks Agreement To Ensure There Is ‘No Further War’

Araghchi added that Iran was seeking an agreement with the U.S. that would ensure that there would be “no further war,” according to the report.

He said that Iran is also seeking guarantees that the U.S. was earnest with respect to negotiations with the country, following multiple instances of both sides going back on their reportedly agreed positions.

Araghchi also clarified that one of Tehran’s red lines is the country keeping its highly enriched uranium, while noting that Iran was open to discussing a “fair solution.”

"I believe a fair solution can be reached ​on the issue of ​nuclear material, one ⁠that is based on our national interests while also meeting the country’s needs," Araghchi said.

Trump Dismisses Iran’s Demands

Addressing reporters on Friday, U.S. President Donald Trump confirmed that Tehran is seeking a deal. However, he poured cold water over hopes of an end to the conflict in the near future.

“They want to make a deal, but they don't want to make a deal that's acceptable to me,” he said.

Meanwhile, a U.S. State Department official told Al Jazeera that the impact of economic pressure on Iran is having a “real impact” on its ability to undertake strikes, while adding that the Trump administration has not yet set a deadline to end the conflict.

The official also stated that Iran is not prepared to agree to the conditions set forth by the U.S. even as it seeks to reach a deal to end the war.

Crude Oil Prices Continue To Cool

Crude oil prices continued to cool this week, with the U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures expiring in January falling 5.6% to $82.4 a barrel after a 2.6% fall the week before.

Brent crude futures expiring in January fell 3.41% this week, hovering around $92.49 a barrel after a 2.51% decline the week before.

The United States Oil Fund ETF (USO) gained about 1% on Friday, while the ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil ETF (UCO) rose about 0.6%.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 1.11%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) rose 1.53%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) surged 0.94%. data.title: Zcash, NEAR Lead Crypto Losses As Anthropic's Market Debut Fails To Spark Risk-On Rally
data.description:
Key points:
  • Zcash fell around 13%, and NEAR fell close over 11% over the past 24 hours.
  • Zcash’s price dip came even as HeartSciences announced the approval of its merger with a Zcash mining company.
  • The losses in Zcash and NEAR’s price came a day after Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq. 

Anthropic's (ANT) market debut failed to provide the risk-on bounce traders were hoping for, leaving Zcash (ZEC) and NEAR Protocol (NEAR) as the biggest losers in crypto.

ZEC dropped nearly 13%, and NEAR fell about 11% on Friday, making them two of the biggest decliners among the largest crypto tokens.

ZEC fell on the same day that there was a push for a new public listing for miners on the network. HeartSciences (HSCS) said on Friday its shareholders had approved its merger with Fortitude Mining Holdings, a Zcash mining company owned by Digital Currency Group (DCG). Some 86% of shareholders voted in favor.

After the deal closes, Nasdaq will list the combined company under the ticker "TUDE." CEO Jaime Leverton said that "the vote clears the way for Fortitude to become a leading publicly traded Zcash mining platform."

Fortitude runs more than 60 megawatts of power capacity across seven U.S. sites. It said it sells or otherwise monetizes all the ZEC it mines, and that DCG and its affiliates also sell ZEC from time to time.

Retail Traders Remain Sour On ZEC

ZEC's price was trading around $730 at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ZEC dropped to the extremely bearish zone from the bearish zone, accompanied by 'normal' chatter levels over the past day.

View this Stocktwits post

On Stocktwits, one user said that ZEC could see $500 soon.

NEAR's price was trading at $2.7 at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around NEAR remained in the 'neutral' zone, with 'normal' chatter levels over the past day.

Arthur Hayes Reverses Bullish Stance After Anthropic IPO

The losses came a day after Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq.

Hayes had treated the listing as a gauge for broader markets. The Flop Labs CEO called Anthropic's IPO "the test" of whether investors were ready to take on risk again. A strong debut, he said, would mean "It's long everything."

The market's reaction changed his mind. "Mrkt no likey the $ANT IPO, I took the L and will wait for a better setup to get long again," Hayes wrote on X on Thursday. That marked a quick reversal.

On Monday, Hayes had named ZEC and NEAR among his "Four Horsemen," a group of tokens he expected to rally before the AI bubble ended.

After the IPO, he wrote, "The Four Horsemen are now decapitated."

ANT stock opened well above its $83 IPO price, then pulled back from its listing-day high.

data.title: Waymo Robotaxis Face 2 Recalls Over Closed Freeway Lane Violations, Traffic Control Issues
data.description:
On Friday, Alphabet Inc.’s self-driving unit Waymo said it is issuing two safety recalls affecting its robotaxis over incidents involving blocked freeway lanes and police-directed traffic control.

Waymo Recalls Robotaxis Over Freeway, Traffic Control Issues

Waymo filed two safety recalls with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) on Thursday, targeting its automated driving system, Reuters reported.

The company said the updates are intended to strengthen how its technology handles “closed freeway lanes and intersections with manual traffic control.”

The first recall addresses unusual situations in which a Waymo vehicle could enter and continue traveling through a closed freeway lane.

The company said no crashes or injuries were reported in these incidents and that it was still developing a remedy.

The second recall focuses on how robotaxis respond to instructions from police officers and emergency personnel at intersections.

The issue followed an incident in which a vehicle obeyed an officer’s directions, but the officer was subsequently temporarily obstructed. Waymo completed a software update addressing the problem on Nov. 6.

Waymo did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.

California Freeway Ban Adds to Waymo’s Safety Troubles

The recalls come after California regulators barred Waymo vehicles from using freeways in the state last week following incidents in which robotaxis entered active construction zones.

Waymo subsequently announced a pause in its U.S. freeway operations earlier this week.

Separately, NHTSA opened a recall query last week involving nearly 3,000 company-owned vehicles after reports that Waymo robotaxis passed stopped school buses displaying flashing red lights.

Investigators are examining whether a software update introduced late last year adequately addressed the issue, particularly since several reported violations occurred after the company said the fix had been deployed.

Additionally, NHTSA and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating a January incident in which a Waymo robotaxi struck a child near an elementary school in Santa Monica, California.

Price Action: On Friday, Alphabet’s Class A shares fell 2.70% to $265.29, while Class C shares declined 2.59% to close at $264, according to Benzinga Pro.

According to Benzinga Edge Stock Rankings, GOOGL ranks in the 16th percentile for Momentum and the 80th percentile for Growth, while its short-, medium- and long-term price trends remain negative.

data.title: Natco Pharma gets seven observations after USFDA inspection at Hyderabad plant
data.description:
Natco Pharma has received seven observations from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) following an inspection of its formulations manufacturing facility in Kothur, Hyderabad.

The inspection was conducted between November 12 and November 20, 2026. The observations were issued in Form 483, which the US FDA uses to communicate concerns identified during inspections of manufacturing facilities.

Natco Pharma said it believes the observations are procedural in nature and is confident of addressing them within the stipulated timelines.

"The Company believes that the observations are procedural in nature and is confident of addressing these observations comprehensively within stipulated timelines," it said in an exchange filing on November 21.

The inspection covered the company's formulations manufacturing facility, which makes finished pharmaceutical products. The company did not provide details of the seven observations in its filing.

A Form 483 is issued when FDA investigators identify conditions that may violate regulatory requirements during an inspection. It is not the same as a warning letter or a final regulatory decision. Companies are generally expected to respond to the observations and explain the corrective steps they plan to take.

Headquartered in Hyderabad, Natco Pharma develops and manufactures generic and branded medicines, speciality pharmaceuticals and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). It has manufacturing facilities approved by several regulatory authorities, including the US FDA, Brazil's ANVISA, Health Canada and the World Health Organization.

data.title: Dan Ives Calls AI Sell-Off One Of The Most ‘Disconnected’ In His Career, Says Wall Street Is Acting Like AI Is Dead — ‘This Is A Generational Opportunity’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ives said the recent downturn has been among the most disconnected technology sell-offs he's witnessed, arguing that investor expectations have swung sharply against the AI industry.
  • The tech bull believes the AI investment cycle remains in its early stages, with the market overlooking the long-term potential of companies positioned to benefit from the technology.
  • Ives acknowledged that the market is grappling with a combination of political uncertainty, China-related concerns and the potential impact of restrictions on AI chip exports.

Wall Street's AI trade is facing another bout of turbulence, but Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives isn't backing away from his bullish thesis. The tech bull sees the latest sell-off as an overreaction to uncertainty surrounding AI spending, chip demand and the political backlash against data center expansion.

During an interview with CNBC on Friday, Ives said the market is increasingly pricing in a scenario in which the AI revolution simply doesn't happen.

Ives Calls AI Sell-Off One Of The Most 'Disconnected' He's Seen

Ives said the recent downturn has been among the most disconnected technology sell-offs he's witnessed throughout his career, arguing that investor expectations have swung sharply against the AI industry.

"These stocks are almost pricing in that the AI revolution doesn't happen, that it basically goes away," he said.

Ives said he believes the AI investment cycle remains in its early stages, with the market overlooking the long-term potential of companies positioned to benefit from the technology.

"And if you believe… and I believe we are less than 15% through… this is going to be a generational opportunity to buy the winners here," he said.

He added that he has been guiding investors through the volatility, describing the current sell-off as one of the most unusual disconnects between market sentiment and the underlying technology opportunity he has seen since beginning his career in the late 1990s.

"This is not the end. This is just a turbulent, scary time for investors where it's all kind of come to a head here," Ives said.

Nvidia, AI Chips And Data Center Demand Still Have Ives Convinced

Ives acknowledged that the market is grappling with a combination of political uncertainty, China-related concerns and the potential impact of restrictions on AI chip exports.

But he argued that chip demand remains considerably stronger than investors may appreciate, suggesting Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) could be facing underestimated demand.

"If you want to order a chip today, you're probably not getting it until the end of 2028," Ives said.

He also pushed back against concerns that opposition to data center construction could derail the AI build-out, saying roughly 75% of projects are already permitted.

"I just think we are going through so much uncertainty and I get it. But when the reality… when we look past… I think a year and a half from now, we're going to look at this and the market got this way wrong relative to what's priced in here,” he said.

Ives reiterated that he believes the AI revolution is far from over. "And I don't believe it's done, it's just getting started," he said.

Ives Sees A Multiyear Tech Bull Market Despite AI Stock Rout

Ives' latest remarks echo his broader bullish outlook, when he argued earlier this month that the technology bull market remains intact despite market turbulence following the U.S. midterm elections.

Ives described the political backlash against data center development as a major shock to technology investors.

"I think it's the blue tidal wave that was really the gut punch to tech investors because of the anti-AI data center push," he said.

Ives also argued that the market had gone too far in treating shifts in capital spending and political opposition as signs that AI was nearing its end.

"The stocks reflect some of that, but I think where this got over its skis is that this sell-off is almost treating AI like it's done. Like, it's not gonna happen," he said.

Ives believes the AI infrastructure boom could benefit companies well beyond semiconductor makers, including energy, industrials and financial services.

Ultimately, Ives said he remains convinced that the broader technology bull market is intact, describing the recent turbulence as "just a white-knuckle roller-coaster scary moment."

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 1.11%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) rose 1.53%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) surged 0.94%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) declined over 6% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) fell nearly 7%.

data.title: Bitcoin falls to more than 2-year low as global markets sink
data.description:
Bitcoin fell to the lowest level in over two years, extending its reversal from market darling after the re-election of Donald Trump to a casualty of a broader retreat from speculative bets.

The original cryptocurrency slumped 6% in the US on Friday and another 5.7% in Asia on Saturday to $55,533, its weakest since September 2024. It has lost more than half its value since reaching a peak above $126,000 in October 2025 and is now worth less than it was when crypto-friendly Trump retook the White House.

Bitcoin has been caught in a confluence of pressures in recent weeks. A hack of Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, at the end of October rattled digital assets, while sweeping Democratic victories in the US midterm elections the following week fueled concerns that the crypto industry’s push for friendlier rules has lost momentum.

“The broader market has shifted into a sharp lack of confidence, and investors are de-risking,” said Andy Baehr, managing director of asset management at GSR. “Bitcoin is along for the ride here, typically weak in deleveraging environments.”

The latest leg lower has been fueled by investors pulling money from Bitcoin exchange-traded funds amid an unraveling of the artificial-intelligence trade. Bitcoin ETFs have seen year-to-date outflows of more than $3 billion.

The broader backdrop is becoming less favorable as well. For much of the past decade, cryptocurrencies occupied a privileged place in the risk-taking economy. Now a stronger dollar and rising expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase are adding to the pressure.

The market is pricing a more aggressive Fed rate hike and a slowdown in the AI buildout, prompting “an excessively negative market interpretation right now,” said Fabian Dori, chief investment officer at Sygnum Bank.

On Friday, Bitcoin’s slide triggered the liquidation of roughly $2 billion in long crypto bets over 24 hours, with Bitcoin positions accounting for the majority of that sum, according to Coinglass data.

“What made the move so fast was leverage,” said Andrew Yang, research analyst at Kaiko. “As Nasdaq losses deepened again in late-morning New York trading, Bitcoin broke below $60,000, triggering $94.6 million in BTC liquidations on Binance, Bybit and OKX in a single hour.”

The downturn is unfolding at what should have been a triumphant moment for the industry.

With Trump as US president, crypto has secured many of the victories it spent the better part of a decade pursuing: a sympathetic White House, friendlier regulators, institutional acceptance and a legislative framework that increasingly treats digital assets as a permanent part of the financial system. Yet rather than unleashing a new wave of demand, those milestones have coincided with one of Bitcoin’s deepest retreats in years.

Earlier crypto crashes were punctuated by spectacular failures or waves of forced selling. This downturn has been marked by a steadier erosion in demand. Bitcoin fell even as inflation worries mounted, doing little to bolster its case as a hedge. And when geopolitical turmoil sent investors looking for safety, they turned to traditional havens.

Institutional acceptance hasn’t gone away, but the early enthusiasm has cooled. The question now is whether the biggest buyers will keep adding to their holdings at the pace the industry once expected.

data.title: Reported Bosch-TCS Deal Could Involve 3,000 Employees; Bosch Yet To Confirm
data.description:
The reported transaction could involve part of Bosch's India technology and product development operations, but neither company has confirmed the discussions

Bosch Group in India has declined to comment on reports that Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is in discussions to acquire part of its India technology and product development operations, a potential transaction that could involve the transfer of up to 3,000 employees.In a statement shared in response to the reports, Bosch said it was refraining from commenting on market speculation and unverified statements.“In reference to the recent news articles published around the potential sale of part of Bosch India operations, we would like to clearly state that Bosch Group in India refrains from commenting on market speculations and unverified statements,” the company said.

The statement follows a report by Mint published on 19 November, which said TCS was in early discussions to acquire a portion of Bosch’s India technology and product development operations. The report suggested that the discussions could move to the board level next month, although the scope and terms of a potential transaction remain unclear.Bosch has not confirmed whether negotiations are underway or whether a transaction is being considered. The reported employee transfer and the number of employees potentially affected also remain unverified.

What The Reported Deal Could Involve

According to Mint, the proposed transaction could cover part of Bosch’s technology and product development operations in India, with up to 3,000 employees potentially moving to TCS.

The discussions are reportedly linked to Bosch’s cost-containment efforts and the possible transfer of certain technology and product development activities. For TCS, the acquisition could expand its engineering workforce and capabilities in areas such as physical artificial intelligence (AI), which involves the application of AI in physical systems, including robots and autonomous vehicles.However, neither company has confirmed the reported scope of the discussions or the potential terms of an agreement.

Bosch's Technology Operations In India

Bosch established its technology operations in India in Bengaluru in 1997 through Bosch Global Software Technologies (BGSW), subsequently expanding its presence to Hyderabad, Pune and Coimbatore.Mint's report cited a global workforce of 28,900 employees across Bosch's global capability centre (GCC) network, with India accounting for approximately four-fifths of that workforce. Bengaluru reportedly accounts for around half of the employees in the network.

The reported transaction concerns Bosch's technology and product development operations and is distinct from the business of listed Bosch , the automotive components manufacturer in India.

TCS's Push Into Captive Technology Centres

The reported discussions come amid TCS's efforts to expand its technology and engineering capabilities through acquisitions and partnerships involving captive technology centres.Recent transactions cited in the report include the acquisition of Best Buy's India technology centre in October and the acquisition of Porsche's consulting subsidiary MHP for US$373 million in August. TCS also secured a five-year, US$1.45 billion contract for Porsche's IT modernisation.

Acquiring captive technology operations can give IT services companies access to established engineering teams, specialised capabilities and long-term client engagements. However, integrating such teams can also present operational and cost challenges, particularly when employee compensation structures differ from those of the acquiring organisation.

For now, the reported Bosch-TCS discussions remain unconfirmed. Bosch's statement does not establish whether negotiations are taking place, leaving the potential transaction, employee movement and scope of operations uncertain.

data.title: ‘Axis Bank’s MSME Book Has Grown 24 Per Cent CAGR Over Five To Six Years’: Prashanth T.S.
data.description:
The bank is focusing on cash-flow-based lending, working capital and supply chain financing to support MSME growth, while expanding its engagement with women-led businesses, says Prashanth T.S., Group Head – Mid-Corporate & Medium Enterprises Group, Axis Bank

On the occasion of Women's Entrepreneurship Day on November 19, 2026, Axis Bank held a media briefing in New Delhi to discuss the evolving MSME landscape and the growing contribution of women-led businesses to India's economy. The discussion focused on the financing needs of women entrepreneurs, access to formal credit, working capital requirements, collateral-related challenges and the role of banking institutions in supporting business growth and expansion.

In an interaction with BW Businessworld, Prashanth T.S., Group Head – Mid-Corporate & Medium Enterprises Group, Axis Bank, discussed the bank's MSME lending growth, changing borrowing patterns and opportunities in the Delhi-NCR market. He also shared insights into the bank's approach to cash-flow-based lending, supply chain financing and its strategy to support MSMEs as they scale their businesses.

Edited Excerpts

Q. How has Axis Bank's MSME lending business been performing, and what kind of growth are you seeing this year?

Axis Bank's MSME business has been performing well. If you look at the performance of our MSME book over the last five to six years, we have grown at around 24 per cent CAGR. This is a business we want to continue growing because it meets the bank's requirements in terms of profitability as well as credit standards.

Q. Are businesses currently borrowing more for expansion, working capital requirements or setting up new facilities?

It is a combination of all these requirements. As businesses grow, their working capital needs also increase, and we participate in meeting those requirements.

In terms of term loans, companies are primarily investing in additional production lines or undertaking smaller expansions within existing facilities. There is no major capital expenditure activity happening at present, but investments are taking place, particularly towards incremental expansion.

Q. Delhi-NCR has a large base of MSMEs. What kind of lending opportunities are you seeing in this market?

There are quite a lot of opportunities. The fact that we are organising this event in Delhi-NCR reflects the importance of this market for us. Our market share here is higher than our overall market share across the bank. This region contributes substantially to our business and will continue to remain a focus market.

Q. Are you seeing an increase in borrowing activity among women-led businesses? How has this segment evolved for the bank?

I would not say there has been a meaningful increase in borrowing activity, but there has been a meaningful increase in entrepreneurial activity. The number of businesses being started by women and the number of women entering entrepreneurship have certainly gone up.

As a bank, we are making efforts to ensure that we provide the support required to help women become entrepreneurs and build successful businesses.

Q. Women entrepreneurs often face challenges related to collateral and establishing a strong credit history. How does the bank approach such cases?

I would not differentiate between women-oriented businesses and other businesses. All MSMEs face challenges when it comes to collateral. That is why we have moved from collateral-based lending to cash-flow-based lending.

I think this gives businesses additional headroom when they are looking for finance.

Q. How important has supply chain financing become for MSMEs, particularly those working with large corporates?

It is very important. Most MSMEs supply goods or services to mid-sized or large corporates, and the key issue is receiving payments. Although there is a government regulation that requires MSME payments to be made within 45 days of invoicing, payments can sometimes get delayed, or businesses may need the money earlier.

This is where banks help through supply chain financing solutions. MSMEs can get their invoices discounted and receive funds earlier.

Q. What are the key areas of focus for Axis Bank's MSME business over the next 12 months?

We want to become an end-to-end banking partner for MSMEs. We do not want to be just lenders. We want to be bankers to these businesses, whether it is providing loans at the beginning, supporting their personal banking requirements or acting as advisors.

Our objective is to help these companies grow and become the mid-sized or large corporates of tomorrow.

data.title: Dalmia Cement Appoints Sunayana Basu As East-Central Talent Acquisition Lead
data.description:
The HR professional brings over a decade of experience across talent acquisition, HR business partnering and recruitment operations

Dalmia Cement (Bharat) Limited has appointed Sunayana Basu as Talent Acquisition Lead – East & Central, strengthening its regional recruitment leadership as the company focuses on its workforce requirements across the two regions.

Basu brings more than a decade of experience across talent acquisition, HR business partnering, recruitment and human resources operations. She joins Dalmia Cement from Nuvoco Vistas Corp. Ltd., where she served as Senior Manager – HR Business Partner for more than three years in Kolkata.

Before joining Nuvoco Vistas, Basu spent over five years with Dalmia Bharat Group, handling Talent Acquisition – East. Her earlier association with the group gives her familiarity with its organisational environment and regional recruitment requirements.

She has also held HR positions at Future Group and Pantaloons, where she gained experience in human resources management and people operations. Earlier in her career, she worked with Lafarge India Pvt. Ltd. as an HR Administrator in Kolkata for more than three years.

In her new role, Basu will lead talent acquisition for the East and Central regions, drawing on her experience in regional recruitment, HR business partnering and workforce management to support the company's hiring priorities.

Dalmia Bharat is among India's established cement manufacturers, with an installed cement manufacturing capacity of 54.7 million tonnes per annum across 19 plants in 12 states.

data.title: 2.5 Lakh Bank Staff To Strike Against IDBI Sale
data.description:
IDBI Bank strike on December 3 will see around 2.5 lakh bank employees protest against the proposed stake sale to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings

Three bank employee and officer unions have called a nationwide strike on December 3 to protest against the proposed sale of a 60 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings. The move escalates opposition to the transaction, which has already faced protests from IDBI Bank employees and political parties.

Around 2.5 lakh employees and officers represented by the All India Bank Employees' Association (AIBEA), the All India Bank Officers' Association (AIBOA) and the Bank Employees Federation of India (BEFI) are expected to participate in the strike, according to a joint statement issued by the unions.

The unions described the proposed sale to a foreign investor as unwarranted and said the transaction would transfer an Indian bank into foreign ownership. The strike call is in support of the United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees (UFIOE), which has also opposed the proposed disinvestment.

Unions Raise Concerns Over Privatisation

The unions described IDBI Bank as a profitable institution, with deposits of around Rs 3.5 lakh crore and advances of approximately Rs 2.5 lakh crore. They argued that public sector banks play an important role in safeguarding people's savings and opposed the transfer of public sector lenders into private hands.

The joint statement also called for the nationalisation of private banks rather than the privatisation of public sector lenders. The latest strike announcement follows a two-day protest by IDBI Bank employees and officers on November 2 and 3 against the proposed stake sale.

The Congress-led Opposition has separately questioned the valuation of IDBI Bank and demanded that the government halt the transaction and constitute a Joint Parliamentary Committee to investigate the process. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleged that the acquisition involved the use of funds belonging to the bank itself, a claim that has been raised as part of the political opposition to the deal.

Fairfax Deal Involves Rs 53,000 Cr Transaction

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax on October 14. The Canadian investor will acquire the government's 30.48 per cent stake, valued at around Rs 26,620 crore, and LIC's 30.24 per cent holding, valued at approximately Rs 26,440 crore.

Led by billionaire Prem Watsa, Fairfax has agreed to pay Rs 81 per share, above the benchmark fair value of Rs 75.99 determined by two independent valuation agencies. The transaction would make Fairfax the promoter of IDBI Bank upon completion.

The deal is expected to be completed by the end of the current financial year, subject to regulatory clearances from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The proposed sale marks a significant step in the government's banking disinvestment process, even as employee unions continue to press for the transaction to be withdrawn.

data.title: DGR Organises Job Fair for Ex-Servicemen in Gurugram
data.description:
Over 868 veterans participate in the employment initiative, with 56 national and multinational companies offering more than 2,544 job opportunities across diverse sectors.

The Directorate General Resettlement (DGR), under the Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare (DESW), Ministry of Defence, organised an Ex-Servicemen (ESM) Job Fair at 54 Air Stores Park (ASP), Air Force Station, Gurugram, on Friday. The initiative witnessed participation from over 868 Ex-Servicemen and 56 leading national and multinational companies, which collectively offered more than 2,544 employment opportunities across various sectors.

The job fair was inaugurated by Pravin Agrawal, Joint Secretary (ESW), in the presence of Ramesh K, Director General, Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM), who attended as the Corporate Guest of Honour. The dignitaries interacted with participating veterans and corporate representatives and appreciated the initiative's role in facilitating the professional transition of former Armed Forces personnel into the corporate sector.

Several prominent organisations participated in the event, including CBRE Group, DLF, Big Bang Boom Solutions, Air India SATS, JCB, Oberoi Group of Hotels, Droneverse, Paltech Cooling Towers & Equipments, Relaxo Footwears, Somany Ceramics, Checkmate Security Services, KEI Industries, Kaytent and Multicolour Steels India, among others.

The job fair provided a common platform for employers and Ex-Servicemen to connect and explore employment opportunities. It enabled veterans to showcase their technical expertise, leadership qualities, managerial capabilities and administrative experience. At the same time, participating companies gained access to a skilled and experienced workforce with strong organisational and operational capabilities.

Through such initiatives, DGR continues to facilitate employment opportunities and second careers for retiring and retired Armed Forces personnel. These efforts support their transition into civilian life while enabling industries to benefit from the professional experience, discipline and skills acquired during military service.

The initiative also reinforces the Ministry of Defence's commitment to the welfare, resettlement and empowerment of Ex-Servicemen by strengthening partnerships between the Armed Forces veteran community and corporate India.

data.title: COIN Stock Falls To Lowest Level Since 2023 After Exchange Seeks CFTC Clarity On Sports, Election Contracts
data.description:
Key points:
  • Coinbase shares fell more than 20% this week.
  • The company has asked the CFTC to treat sports and election event contracts as swaps under federal commodities law.
  • The exchange warned that conflicting state gambling laws and court rulings are disrupting prediction markets, fragmenting liquidity and making it harder for traders to hedge.

Shares of Coinbase (COIN) closed on Friday at their lowest level since 2023, down 20% for the week. The exchange lobbied the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) for stricter federal rules on sports and election contracts.

The stock fell 6.3% below its February 2024 low. It ended the day at $127.65 on Nov. 13. The decline continued a slide that had already taken COIN to new two-year lows earlier this month.

COIN stock was up over 0.3% in overnight trading. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around COIN remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘normal’ chatter levels over the past day.

Coinbase Backs CFTC Proposal

In a comment letter published Wednesday, Coinbase said it “strongly supports” the CFTC’s proposal to define such contracts as swaps. Coinbase argued that the law already treated these contracts as swaps, so a final rule would confirm existing law and not create new law. The firm described that extra layer of certainty as "belt and suspenders."

Coinbase argued these contracts already count as swaps under federal commodities law. Spelling that out would reduce uncertainty where "state actions and conflicting judicial decisions have created unnecessary confusion," the exchange said.

The letter arrives as the debate heats up over who should regulate prediction markets. Other states, including Utah, Arkansas, Maryland and Connecticut, have taken steps to classify contracts for sports events as illegal gambling under their own laws. The CFTC said Nov. 13 that Arkansas is the 11th state it has sued to defend its authority over the markets.

This has created "avoidable uncertainty" for exchanges, customers and courts, Coinbase said. Conflicting rulings also split trading and affected liquidity, making it more difficult for traders to hedge, the company said. Coinbase has asked the CFTC to maintain an open-ended list of event categories. It said a fixed list could leave out newer products, including contracts relating to crypto, technology or science.

The exchange also argued that prediction markets are different from betting, and that event contract exchanges match buyers and sellers. The letter noted that sportsbooks and casinos also typically take the other side of a customer's bet as well.

In another letter filed the same day, Coinbase supported a CFTC rule that would exclude casino-style gambling products from the swap definition. And it said the two rules together draw "a workable line" between derivatives markets and gambling.

data.title: Global crude oil prices may fall to $70 by end-2027 as supply surplus looms
data.description:
Global crude oil prices could normalise to around USD 70 per barrel by the end of 2027 as rising non-OPEC+ supplies and declining Chinese oil demand push the market into a surplus, while refining margins are expected to remain elevated in the near term, according to a JM Financial report.

The report, based on an expert session with Iman Nasseri, Senior Vice President for Middle East and Asia at FGE Nexant, said Brent crude could remain high and volatile in the near term before moderating as supply-demand dynamics improve.

Oil market likely to move into surplus

“Global oil demand-supply balance is expected to move into surplus aided by non-OPEC+ supply growth and decline in China’s oil demand,” the report said.

It added that the possibility of an inventory restocking rally supporting oil prices was limited, as China’s purchases were likely to remain gradual once crude prices fell below USD 70 per barrel. The US was also unlikely to replenish its Strategic Petroleum Reserve under the current administration.

US-Iran agreement unlikely in the near term

On the geopolitical front, a US-Iran agreement remains unlikely in the near term, although a resolution could become more probable by mid-2027 amid increasing economic pressure on Iran.

Nasseri said a deal was unlikely without a regime change in either country, adding that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) continued to maintain strong control over Iran despite economic pressure.

Meanwhile, crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea have recovered to around 90 per cent of pre-war levels, supported by risk-tolerant vessels, exemptions for Iraqi and select Chinese cargoes, and transit payments by Gulf countries for safe passage.

Refining margins to remain elevated

The report said diesel supply constraints were likely to keep refining margins and product cracks stronger for longer, with gradual normalisation expected by the end of 2027.

“Refining margins and product cracks are expected to remain stronger in near-term and gradually normalise by end-CY27,” it said.

Global refinery runs in October 2026 were around 5 million barrels per day below February levels, reflecting lower operations in the Middle East, Russia and China.

LNG prices likely to moderate from second half of 2027

Separately, global liquefied natural gas (LNG) demand is expected to remain tight and prices elevated through the 2026-27 winter. However, additional capacity from the US and Qatar could push the market into surplus and moderate prices from the second half of 2027, the report said.

data.title: Rising capital goods trade, record coastal shipments to drive India's port cargo growth
data.description:
India’s port and cargo activity could remain supported by strong external trade and rising movement of capital goods, although the sharp divergence between container volumes and cargo tonnage points to higher transhipment activity and inflationary pressures, according to a research report by JM Financial.

Aggregate cargo volumes at major and minor ports increased 18.7 per cent year-on-year in October, accelerating from 6.3 per cent growth in September, driven by a sharp rise in coastal cargo and overseas shipments, the brokerage said.

“Core EXIM trade growth in Oct’26 was exceptionally strong at 32.7% YoY, led by a sharp uptick in imports/exports of engineering and electronic goods,” the brokerage said in its sector update.

Core exports, excluding petroleum products, gold, silver and precious metals, rose 33.5 per cent year-on-year, while core imports increased 32.1 per cent during the month.

Capital goods trade was a major contributor, with imports rising 36 per cent and exports increasing 44 per cent year-on-year.

Trade growth outpaces container and cargo volumes

The brokerage noted that the growth in core EXIM trade was significantly higher than the 10 per cent increase in aggregate container volumes by tonnage and the 22.5 per cent growth in major port cargo volumes, indicating sharp price inflation, particularly in electronic and engineering goods.

Major ports handled 93.6 million metric tonnes (mmt) of cargo in October, registering 22.5 per cent growth. Coastal cargo volumes reached a record 31.6 mmt, surging 80.8 per cent year-on-year.

“Aggregate port volumes (minor and major) rose 18.7% YoY, led by strong 50.9% YoY growth in coastal cargo and 10.1% YoY growth in overseas volumes in Oct’26,” the report said.

Minor ports handled 68.4 mmt of cargo, up 13.8 per cent, supported by petroleum, oil and lubricants (POL) and coal shipments.

Container volumes rise 26.8 per cent; transhipment activity increases

Container activity also recorded strong growth, with overall container volumes rising 26.8 per cent year-on-year in October. However, container tonnage increased by a comparatively lower 11.8 per cent.

The brokerage attributed the divergence to higher transhipment volumes.

Coal volumes across major and minor ports increased 15.2 per cent to 37.5 mmt, while aggregate iron ore volumes rose 7.8 per cent to 9.4 mmt, indicating broad-based improvement in cargo movement.

data.title: Trump Has A Message for Big Tech Firms Like Amazon, Google and Microsoft Building Data Centers Abroad: ‘We’re Going to Put A Tremendous Tax On Them’
data.description:
President Donald Trump is threatening steep tax penalties on U.S. technology companies that build data centers overseas, signaling a push to keep more AI infrastructure investment within American borders.

Trump Threatens Taxes On Overseas Data Centers

On Friday, speaking at a White House press conference, Trump said his administration would push companies to construct data centers in the U.S. rather than expand their infrastructure abroad, CNBC reported.

"We’re going to fight very hard for the data centers," Trump said before announcing the proposed policy, adding that companies could still build overseas but would face financial consequences.

"They can, but we’re going to put a tremendous tax on them," he warned.

Amazon, Google and Microsoft Could Face Impact

The proposal could affect major U.S. cloud and technology companies, including Amazon.com, Inc. , Alphabet Inc. , Microsoft Corp. , Meta Platforms, Inc. and Oracle Corp. , all of which have established data center operations internationally.

Overseas facilities allow cloud providers to serve customers closer to their locations, improve service performance and comply with local data-storage regulations.

The White House, Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.

Trump’s AI Push Faces Domestic Opposition

Trump’s push for more U.S. data center construction comes as public opposition to the facilities remains significant.

A CNBC All-America Economic Survey found that 64% of registered voters opposed having an AI data center within 10 miles of their homes, while only 13% supported the idea.

Data centers have faced growing scrutiny over their electricity consumption, water requirements, and potential impact on local communities.

Trump Highlights US-China AI Competition

The announcement came a day after Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at a trilateral summit in China.

Trump said Xi had congratulated him on America’s AI progress, adding that the Chinese leader also preferred the term “super intelligence.”

The president also said the U.S. and China could work together on AI safety.

Trump also said that discussions about Nvidia Corp. and Jensen Huang’s alleged ties to a woman accused of spying for China received little attention during his meeting.

This content was partially produced with the help of AI tools and was reviewed and published by Benzinga editors.

data.title: Indonesia's OJK fines and sanctions firms for stock manipulation, disclosure failures
data.description:
Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) on Saturday announced sanctions in 10 capital market violation cases, amid efforts to strengthen enforcement, bolster market integrity and protect investors.

  • OJK ordered the return of 23.77 billion rupiah ($1.30 million) in illicit gains from three stock manipulation cases, involving shares of PT Grand House Mulia Tbk , PT Saraswanti Anugerah Makmur Tbk and PT Suryamas Dutamakmur Tbk

  • In the HOMI case, OJK also ordered the closure of 15 securities accounts linked to the trading activity between March and July 2023

  • The agency also imposed a total of 3.71 billion rupiah ($203,176) in administrative fines on seven listed companies for disclosure failures, material and affiliated-party transaction breaches, financial reporting violations and non-compliance with share transfer obligations

  • OJK also barred multiple individuals involved in the manipulation cases from participating in Indonesia's capital markets, derivatives and carbon exchange sectors for periods ranging from 3 to 10 years

  • OJK previously sanctioned three listed firms as part of Indonesia's market reforms following concerns raised by global index providers over the transparency and investability of Indonesia's capital markets

($1 = 18,260.0000 rupiah)

data.title: Iraq fire at Basra power station kills at least four, injures 30
data.description:
At least 4 people were killed and 30 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.

Civil defence teams brought the fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra under control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq's state news agency, INA, reported.

The fire spread to neighbouring houses and forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.

The Hartha station has an installed generating capacity of 800 megawatts but had been operating at around 400 megawatts before the fire, they said.

There was no immediate official information on the cause of the fire or the extent of the damage, INA reported.

Iraq's electricity infrastructure has long struggled with decades of underinvestment, inadequate maintenance and an inability to meet peak demand, particularly during the extremely hot summer months. Fires and technical failures at substations and power facilities have previously disrupted electricity supplies and caused widespread outages.

data.title: MKBHD Says He Will Honor Tesla Cybercab’s 2024 Bet, Elon Musk Says ‘Fair Enough’: ‘I Will Accept Delivery…’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Brownlee said he intends to honor the spirit of his earlier bet involving Tesla's Cybercab, confirming that he has submitted the deposit and selected Austin, Texas, as his delivery location.
  • He added that he would personally travel to Austin if Tesla is ready to deliver the vehicle.
  • Tesla recently announced that select customers are being invited to purchase the Cybercab for personal use, with the vehicle priced at an estimated $29,990.

Popular tech YouTuber Marques Brownlee, better known as MKBHD, is following through on a long-running bet involving Tesla Inc.'s (TSLA) Cybercab, after the company opened personal orders for its autonomous vehicle.

Brownlee confirmed he has placed an order for the vehicle, prompting CEO Elon Musk to respond briefly but approvingly on social media.

Tesla shares declined nearly 8% in Friday’s regular trading, while gaining about 2% in the afterhours session.

MKBHD Says He'll Follow Through On His Cybercab Bet

Brownlee said he intends to honor the spirit of his earlier bet involving Tesla's Cybercab, confirming that he has submitted the deposit and selected Austin, Texas, as his delivery location.

"I will honor the spirit of the bet. I was invited to buy one, so I did. I submitted my $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and I selected the city of Austin, Texas," Brownlee said in a recent episode of the Waveform podcast.

He added that he would personally travel to Austin if Tesla is ready to deliver the vehicle.

"So if they actually go, 'alright, your Cybercab is ready', I will fly down to Austin, and I will accept delivery of my personal Cybercab,” he added.

Musk responded to Brownlee’s comments in a post on X with two words, “Fair enough.”

The exchange brings the earlier bet back into focus as Tesla begins inviting select customers to purchase the vehicle for personal use, marking a notable step in the company's push toward autonomous transportation.

Tesla Cybercab Personal Orders Come With Restrictions

Tesla recently announced that select customers are being invited to purchase the Cybercab for personal use, with the vehicle priced at an estimated $29,990 and deliveries expected to begin in December.

The offering, however, comes with several restrictions. Buyers must pay a $1,000 non-refundable deposit and a mandatory $299 monthly subscription to operate the vehicle's autonomous driving software.

The Cybercab is a two-seat, two-door vehicle without a steering wheel or pedals, and its personal-use rollout is initially limited to supported geographic areas.

Tesla's order-page fine print specifies that personally owned Cybercabs will operate only in supported service areas, with the initial rollout tied to existing Robotaxi geofenced locations.

The company also restricts buyers from immediately using their personally owned Cybercabs to generate commercial revenue through its ride-hailing network.

Musk Previously Admitted The Cybercab Subscription Fee Was Too High

Brownlee's latest Cybercab post follows an earlier exchange in which he criticized several restrictions on Tesla's personal-use offering, including its invite-only availability, geographic limitations and mandatory monthly subscription.

"Cybercab order page is live. Invite only. Must accept delivery to one of these cities in Texas. Only operates in those existing geofenced areas. Requires a $300 monthly subscription to operate. One vehicle per customer. ‘Estimated delivery’ December," Brownlee previously said.

Musk responded that the vehicle would eventually become available nationwide, subject to regulatory approval, while acknowledging that the monthly fee was too expensive.

"But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month," Musk said.

The acknowledgment suggests Tesla could eventually reduce the Cybercab's monthly operating fee from roughly $299 to around $115, although Musk did not provide a timeline.

Tesla's Robotaxi service initially launched with Model Y SUVs in Austin in June 2025 before expanding to other locations in Texas and Florida. Musk has also previously said Tesla owners could eventually make their vehicles available through a broader autonomous ride-hailing network.

What Retail Investors Think Of TSLA Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Tesla trended in the ‘neutral’ territory at the time of writing.

TSLA stock is down 23% year-to-date and 13% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is up 6% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 4%.
